_comment: client-error-monitor.yml checks in to a Sentry cron monitor every run.
The monitor notices a check-in that does not arrive, which is the only
thing watching whether that workflow still runs at all - GitHub drops
scheduled runs silently rather than queueing them, and disables
schedules on inactive repositories without a word. Until this file, the
monitor noticed and then told nobody: the detector existed and no
workflow listed it. Detection without notification is the shape of bug
this whole epic was opened for.
detectorName is required HERE and absent from the other files in this
directory, and that is not an inconsistency. A workflow binds to a
project through a detector, and apply.sh resolves one by (project,
type). Project 4512075995283456 holds TWO detectors of type
monitor_check_in_failure, one per cron monitor:
10315978  Heartbeat workflow
10315979  Client error monitor workflow   <- this one
so type alone does not identify one. apply.sh refuses rather than
picking; the name is how this file says which. The id is deliberately
not written here for the reason apply.sh's header gives: a number means
nothing to a reviewer and breaks when a project is recreated. The cost
is that renaming the detector in Sentry means renaming it here.
THE HEARTBEAT IS NOT COVERED, and that is a decision rather than an
oversight. Sentry Crons bills per ACTIVE monitor and this org has one
seat, which went to client-error-monitor.yml; heartbeat.yml's check-in
step was removed in PR #163 for that reason and says so at lines 41-69.
Detector 10315978 therefore fronts a monitor that receives nothing and
could never fire. Pointing this workflow at it would produce exactly the
fault the file is meant to fix. Covering the heartbeat means buying a
second seat, not editing this file.
environment is production, like every workflow here, and cron check-ins
do carry one: Sentry's check-in API defaults it to production and
checkin.sh now states it outright rather than relying on that default.
UNVERIFIED: the trigger below. Sentry publishes no schema for these
endpoints (onlooker-txcu.2), and which conditions a
monitor_check_in_failure detector accepts could not be established
offline. first_seen_event is the shape the issue_stream rules here use,
on the reasoning that a missed check-in raises a new issue. If Sentry
rejects it, the response names the valid types and apply.sh prints it;
the next thing to try is an empty conditions array, meaning 'whenever
this detector fires'. Do not treat this alert as load-bearing until it
has been seen to fire - accepting is not firing.
email/issue_owners matches the other files. A missed check-in has no
suspect commit to own it, so it falls through to AllMembers, which is
the intended audience anyway.

workflow.name: Client error monitor missed a check-in (production)
